clue.text: Dares to disrupt when prepared to eat

indicators.note: to disrupt something is to throw it into disorder, so the seven letters of the first two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is goaded into upsetting a meal that is all ready to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of the indicator phrase but belongs to the fodder: DARES + TO gives the seven letters, and 'disrupt' scrambles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that has been cooked in an oven is ready for the table.

clue.text: Polish picture showing an Italian river

parts.note: to rub is to polish
an icon is a religious picture

explanation.surface: Someone shines up a painting of a river in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' disguises itself as the nationality; capitalised at the start of the clue it is simply the verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubicon is the stream in northern Italy that Caesar crossed in 49 BC.

clue.text: Fool a superior officer making a charge

parts.note: an ass is a fool
U means upper-class, socially superior
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A senior officer is made a fool of when he leads a cavalry charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior officer' looks like one phrase but splits into U (upper class) and LT (lieutenant).
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a violent rush upon an enemy, an attack.

clue.text: Tease the non-male member of the family

parts.note: T' is a dialect shortening of the, as in northern English
an aunt is a female relation, the counterpart of an uncle

explanation.surface: Teasing a female relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt someone is to jeer at them provokingly.

clue.text: Action to be taken about land taken away

indicators.note: about means the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: a deed is an action
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Legal action is threatened over a piece of land that has been seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Detracted means took away or diminished, as in detracting from merit.

clue.text: Stay to drink some wine

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: An invitation to linger over a glass of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop or brace, something that holds a structure up.

clue.text: Remained sound, being sober

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for remained is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: stayed means remained

explanation.surface: Someone stayed healthy by keeping off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'healthy' but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid describes a settled, serious, unadventurous manner.

clue.text: Exhausted, so released-but not all at once

definitions.meaning: worn out, finished, with nothing left
let out gradually, as a rope or line is paid out bit by bit

explanation.surface: A tired person lets things go slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A spent person or idea is finished; a fishing line is let out a little at a time.

clue.text: Work on a tree maybe cut where necessary

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon prunes only where needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon operates, making incisions only where the patient requires them.

clue.text: A sailor is given marks

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
gets means is given or receives

explanation.surface: A seaman is awarded points.
explanation.definitionFit: Targets are the marks aimed at in shooting or archery.

clue.text: Little framing is copper and light brown

indicators.note: framing means the first piece goes round the others like a picture frame

parts.note: a little is a bit
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A description of a small picture frame in copper and fawn tones.
explanation.definitionFit: Biscuit is the name of a pale tan colour, like a baked cracker.

clue.text: Non-professional from a dull French back-street

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, not glossy

indicators.note: back tells us the French word for street is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: rue is the French for street, hence 'French' in the clue

explanation.surface: Someone without credentials who comes from a drab side road in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' looks like one word for an alley, but 'back' is the reversal signal and 'French' tells you to use the French word for street.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something for love rather than pay, the opposite of a paid expert.

clue.text: Awfully curt cad or knave perhaps

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rude cad is called a knave, as one might insult a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knave' is not an insult here but the jack in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave (jack), queen and king are the picture cards in a pack, so a knave is one example.

clue.text: Cancel the right to go in peace

indicators.note: to go in means this letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: ease is peace and freedom from worry
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Revoking someone's right to enter in tranquillity.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase writing is to wipe it out, to strike it off.

clue.text: The province of some man-a tall guy

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A region belonging to a lanky fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal was a province of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was formerly one of the four provinces of South Africa.

clue.text: Hot meals, possibly including duck, but quite disgusting

indicators.note: including means the duck letter is put inside the rest
possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: Hot food, maybe with duck on the menu, is revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles HOT MEALS into LATHSOME, and 'including' places O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome provokes intense revulsion.

clue.text: Returning at one and learning craft from a skilled woman

indicators.note: returning means the little word at is written backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
lore is knowledge or learning
SS stands for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: Coming back, someone acquires both knowledge and a trade from an expert woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a skill but is a vessel, SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: A tailoress is a woman trained to make clothes, a dressmaker with tailoring skill.

clue.text: Rude yet popular English sup porter and worker

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the word support, broken in two by the printing; a leg supports a table
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A coarse but well-liked English supporter and labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude here means crude and unrefined, lacking grace.

clue.text: Male servant Handel treated roughly!

parts.note: a man is a manservant

indicators.note: treated roughly means the letters of the composer's name are knocked about

explanation.surface: The composer Handel's valet is accused of mishandling him.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the act: a servant roughing up the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle someone is to push them about with force.

clue.text: Heath is holding up money for a watch-dog

indicators.note: is holding means the first word contains the other

parts.note: a moor is a heath

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Edward Heath is propping up funds for a guard dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' suggests the prime minister but is just moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor keeps watch and warns, a supervisor or overseer.

clue.text: Salt-it will come in bearing tax

indicators.note: will come in means it enters the other letters

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: A salt duty is introduced on a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid.

clue.text: Second cereal after tasty Start

indicators.note: after means the grain comes behind the first letter
the start of the word tasty is its first letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A breakfast with cereal coming next after a tasty opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is a moment, an instant as brief as a second.

clue.text: Getting irate in forced inactivity

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: Becoming angry at being made idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, a reluctance to move or act.

clue.text: A flower opening wide in the end

definitions.text: A flower opening wide in the end

parts.words: A flower opening wide in the end
parts.note: a flower seems to be a bloom, but read as something that flows, a river, which broadens where it meets the sea

explanation.surface: A bloom finally unfurling its petals.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the widening tidal mouth of a river.

clue.text: Nick is not going to church

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Nick is skipping church.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or groove in an edge.

clue.text: Dealing with someone who is patient?

definitions.text: Dealing with someone who is patient?

parts.words: Dealing with someone who is patient?
parts.note: the surface suggests dealing with a tolerant person; read instead as what a doctor gives a patient, or as handling someone

explanation.surface: Coping with a person who has great forbearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is both the way one handles a person and medical care given to someone ill.

clue.text: Not all waitresses are required to cover their hair

indicators.note: not all means only part of the word is used, the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Some serving staff must wear hairnets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: The topic for discussion is the state

parts.note: taken as written
ME is the abbreviation for Maine, a US state

explanation.surface: The subject under debate is the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a subject for talk or writing.

clue.text: A tree so well-set produces beautiful blossom

indicators.note: well-set suggests the letters are set out anew, arranged in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A properly planted tree yields lovely flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a garden rose with a scent said to resemble tea, prized for its flowers.

clue.text: Drivers' organisation holding people back-it's such idiocy!

indicators.note: holding means the motoring body's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motorists' breakdown organisation
men are people

indicators.note: back means the word it is read in reverse

parts.note: the word it, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A motoring club keeps people waiting, a piece of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Amentia is an old medical term for severe mental deficiency, a lack of intellect.

clue.text: Turns for information about Oriental jackets

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the letter

parts.note: one who turns to a source for information refers to it
E stands for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone consults a source on Eastern coats.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a short double-breasted coat of thick cloth worn by sailors.

clue.text: People in general split by strike will get 23 across

indicators.note: split by means the first word is broken open with the second put inside

parts.note: they is used for people in general, as in 'they say'
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: A workforce divided by industrial action will receive treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout but means a blow. The definition refers to the answer at 23 across, a word for medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is remedial medical care, the same sense as the cross-referenced light.
